As a hardcore gamer, a veteran competitive gamer (for fighting games), and a budding/amateur game designer/developer; Skullgirls is a great fighting game and a love letter to the fans of the fighting game genre as well as a solid display of artistic prowess. While the actual art direction is very love/hate for a huge majority of users, very few people with an aptitude for animation and an eye for detail will deny that Skullgirls' lacks in either category. Myself included.
On the Art side, the fan-service laden game, while not my cup of tea, earns my respect because of the painstaking work that went into animation the whole game as well as the very detailed background art (that works in on a 3-dimensional scale!) The life and personality that is sewn into each character is easy to see, read, and understand and it doesn't require you to tilt your head to try to "get it." It's a testament to the art side of Skullgirls.
The combination of a western based art-style with eastern influence allows Skullgirls a familiar vibe to those who are fans of Eastern Animation (specifically Anime), while not completely going "full anime" and retaining a visible base within the Western style (i.e. Cartoons).
It's all very good in a technical sense, but as I've said, due to, what I feel is, excessive fan-service, a lot of the technical efforts and achievements (60FPS ANIMATION!) that Skullgirls is filled with goes over the head of an uncomfortable amount of people because they cannot take a more objective stance and look past the fan-service to see how good the art is. Which is a shame, but also understandable because again; what I feel is that this game has a lot of fan-service and if you combine this with the obvious anime influence, a lot of people WILL turn tail or stick their nose up before they can take in the meat and potatoes of Skullgirl's art. I am not of this particular group as I do enjoy anime, but it's clear as day to me as to why so many people can look at Skullgirls for 5 minutes, and trash on the art direction.
Art and Aesthetics aside, let's move on to the rest of the game.
The gameplay of Skullgirls is phenomenal. It hasn't ALWAYS BEEN this great, but because of the patience, and dedication of Mike Z as well as the fighting community of Skullgirls, it's gameplay, I feel, has been steadily rising since it's initial release and especially since the first patch of the game. Unfortunately, a problem that does crop up with the user-base from time to time is the frequency of patches, and the degree of how much the game is changed per patch.
There are 2 versions of Skullgirls on Steam. This one, and the ∞Endless Beta∞ version. A lot of experimental changes show up first on the Endless Beta, and the community and Mike Z collaborate on the effects of said changes and over time, which ever changes are finalized, are then applied to the stable version (this one). As such, the game can feel like, that after a patch, it's a brand new game. This bothers people from time to time because some amount of time they put into the game becomes moot. Be wary of this POTENTIAL when purchasing Skullgirls. There is a need for tolerance for this. The frequency of these changes are not always big and are usually not too significant, and they're growing more infrequent as the game is refined, so while I'm not saying this shouldn't be a concern, the worry and uncertainty this causes should be miniscule.
Moving on, a common (and less true with very patch) complaint is that this game is "learn your 99hit combos that 0-Death everyone". As mentioned, this game is patched actively (does not mean frequently) and this issue has grown to be less and less of concern. Compared to the initial release of Skullgirls, this version is much less laden with lengthy combos. HOWEVER, because the gameplay targets primarily a hardcore demographic, one must realize that against people who are of a higher skill level and with a lack of comeback mechanics (think MvC3 XFACTOR), that it is VERY easy to get overwhelmed and be UNAWARE of the options one has at any given moment and this game allows one to be extremely "dirty" and "out-right mean" because of said skill gap. Contrary to popular belief with the uneducated, there are infinites in this game BUT there is an infinite protection/prevention system that renders these infinites invalid/moot. The system is called "IPS (Infinite Prevention System)". Playing through the tutorial will teach you about it, and if it's not enough, there are tons of videos to help understanding.
Speaking of Online, being one of the first fighting games to officially support and integrate GGPO. Skullgirls online multiplayer is superb. It is not perfect, so please do not treat it as such or think it as such. GGPO also does not mean "Lagless Online" in the way that you may think. While it might cut down input lag (that delayed button press feeling), it "replaces" input lag with something called "Rollbacks". Look it up! Either way, the online is a great step in the right direction, and it earns my praise from that.
The tutorial, in my opinion, is the best tutorial to grace fighting games in the history of forever. With BlazBlu coming in a close second. Skullgirls tutorial equips the true novice of fighting games with a basic fundamental grasp of fighting games at a tournament level, which is invaluable for ALL fighting games. Not only that, but it teaches them about Skullgirls specific things, such as IPS, giving the user the basic amount of knowledge they need to practice Skullgirls on almost every level. From that point onwards, it's up to the user to take themselves to the next level and learn the ins-and-outs of Skullgirls so that they can compete. Unfortunately, there isnt anything like a Trials mode, (though there is an online practice/training mode. Not sure of that's in Endless Beta or both version however. Double Check this!) so outside of Training/Arcade/Story mode, this isnt much practice or practical knowledge a user is given within the game itself, and those wanting to improve have to either grind it out and find out on their own, or go to the official Skullgirls community forum and engage in research and discussion.
The gameplay itself. Ohh sweet doggie. The gameplay. Lot's of fun. On so many levels. Don't let my activity on this version or Endless Beta fool you. I own this game on PS3 and 360 and I have since day 1 on console release. This game is stupid amounts of fun, especially now. While it's a 6 button game, don't let this overwhelm you. It allows for a lot of creativity, and all the actions you think a VS fighter would have, Skullgirls has (At least, most of them). The animations are fluid. The attacks have usefulness. There is a good deal of creativity involved. The lack of comeback mechanics makes this a very skill based game. With the right team, and knowledge, you can easily overwhelm the opponent (double edge sword, but hey!). Despite the fact there are 9 (10 with Endless Beta) characters, there is still a good deal of variety to be had with the team mechanics which allow you to pick a team of up to 3 different characters. While the balance isnt perfect, it's steadily progressing there. Feel free to pick who you want, but do realize that some characters/teams will make the climb to the top a lot harder. Luckily, the mechanics within the game allow you the ability to neutralize this disadvantage if you use it better than the opponent.
Either way, this game is a great buy if you're a fan of the fighting game series. Just realize, that despite this, it's easily possible that you're just not a fan of how it plays. There are dozens of great games that people just don't like for personal taste-based reasons. Skullgirls is not immune to it. As such, while I do recommend this game with my whole being, do a bit of snooping before you buy without thinking. :V

Truly, a wonderful game all around! A well thought out crafting system, as well as a simple but very original rules set. This game belongs on my short list of games that I would recommend to any RPG lover.

This game takes the old-school CRPG system and just does it right. Complete freedom to customize your characters, not restrained to specific classes.  Any character can learn any skill, so you can create hybrid classes just the way you want them.  Conversation and interaction play a huge role, so it's worthwhile to pay some attention to personality skills too.  Combat is much more similar to the original Fallout games - turn-based tactical, although it's not restrained to a grid. Flanking, backstab bonuses, line of sight (including whether you have an ally between your archer and your target), and lots more make combat deep and rewarding.
And don't forget about the element interactions - environment and spell effects interact to a major degree.  Enemies standing in a puddle of oil are much more vulnerable to burn damage. Throw a water balloon at an enemy to wet them, and follow up with a lightning attack for bonus damage.  Toss a poison gas grenade at a group of enemies and then hit the volatile gas cloud with a fire arrow for some major explosion damage.  Tons of interactive environmental things - room decorations like crates, barrels, chairs, etc. can be moved and aren't just decoration - in fact, moving these things is sometimes key to solving puzzles or progressing.
Even more mundane things like equipment repair, rare object identification, crafting, and all of that are handled very well.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who was a fan of games like Baldur's Gate, Planescape Torment, or the old-school Fallout games.

Absolutely beautiful game -- loved the music and artistic style. Point and click puzzles were highly engaging, always different, but never *too* difficult. Timing-based combat system was also very interesting to see, and not ridiculously challenging compared to the rest of the game. Difficulty ramped nicely through the overall game, and the Lunar Puzzle-- that was truly fascinating! It was really enjoyable for me to wait until the real-life moon was in a particular phase before new content was available. Games that attempt to connect to the real world that way aren't seen nearly as often as they should be. I loved the overall casual style of writing in the game; "adventure time grown up" is a rough description of how it felt to me. The characters were really interesting, and some of the things they "thought" (as viewed through another in-game mechanic) were really funny to see. And of course, the Scythian is a great example of a female protagonist whose gender has no bearing on the plot, which is highly refreshing, if you ask me. The ending was slightly dissapointing to me, but nothing that the story didn't set up already. All in all, a game very much worth playing. It makes me very curious to see what Superbrothers comes up with next!

The gameplay elements based on the current (real-time) lunar phase was a neat mix.  The one caveat I would add is that combat can be challenging; there isn't a lot of combat overall (it's mostly a puzzle game), but combat does require some good timing and was harder than I was expecting from an otherwise casual game.  If you enjoy puzzle games, I'd definitely recommend trying Superbrothers: Sword & Sworcery EP, especially if you can catch it on sale.

Pros:
Difficulty- This game has a Simple to Learn Hard to master sort of difficulty where you even have the ability to take what you know from one savegame and use it in another.
Management- Rhe game has a great management system where you can kinda see how difficult making a game, hiring staff, paying upkeep, ect. can really be.
Historic- This game has a "pretty accurate" tale of how gaming has taken place over the years and what the future of gaming could hold.
Replayability- This game makes TONS of referances to other popular games and gaming devices, but has a decent amount of replayability thanks to all the achievments, Consoles, Generes, and mods.
Cons:
Apeal: This is not a Hardore game. Its a game made for Average/Casual gamers alike Remeber this Before you Buy.
SaveGames- Unfortunally this Game does not let you delete savegames only create new save ttill you run out of slots then you can save over prevous saves.
Others- This game may make it dificult to make you favorite companies. (i.e. nintendo and not bieng able to make platforming games.) no Competition from other companies. (yes there ard mods for that thought) and this aspect doesn't Personally bother me but may make the game "Too Easy" for some.
Critics- This Game much Like the Real World has Very Harse Reviewers that can Make or Break your company.
Overall I've Had Way TOO much fun playing this game without mods and Will DEFINITELY Buy the Sequel If They Ever Choose To Make One. :)  -10/10 KhanceGames

Sproggiwood is indeed, a cute game like many have said.  In case you can't tell from the screenshots, this is a mobile port.  The buttons in game are overly large and even some settings still say swipe.
As a rogue-lite game, Sproggiwood is....competent.  There are several upgrades you can do to your village which affects how you play the levels.  The issue is, the levels are barely procedurally generated.  Each level all you will see that is differant is the layout of the vases, webs and traps which a few tile sets being different than the last game you played.  It is pretty lazy.  The monster variety is also pretty lazy.  You have oozes, giant goat men, flying pigs with lasers, flame vampires etc.  The enemy variety is what will exhaust you.  You will witness the same mobs level after level.
I got Sproggiwood on sale.  At 50% off I'd say it's worth it, but definately NOT 15.  There isn't enough content here and the level design is flat and just not that procedural for my liking.  If you're a fan of rogue like games, pass this one up and buy the developer's other game, Caves of Qud if you want a true rogue like dungeon crawler.

The game revolves in the Forced universe. Betadwarf has made two prior games, Forced and Forced Showdown. I have played extensivly Forced Showdown and had alot of fun with it. WIth that in mind I had very high hopes for betadwarfs third game, Minion Masters.
Minion Masters is the PC-variant of Clash Royale were players aquire cards (minions, spells, buildings) and put togethor a deck of 8 cards and battle an random opponent. The goal is to lower the health of the opponents master by 3000 points.
(V.S friend battle is in development).
Tactics and counter knowledge is crucial to be a winner. All new players gets rubies, shards and gold because of the premium upgrade. Rubies are an purchable in-game currency (it is also rewarded by leveling up at certain levels and raise in leauge rank). Shards are also rewarded in the same regard as rubies, but are not purchable and can also be aquired if by spinning the power tower wheel (it is where you spend gold to get a random card). If you get a dublicate card, it is salvaged and you get shards in relation of that cards rarity.
The game is still in beta and under heavy development and balancing. Some cards might be a bit OP. But players with OP cards that plays badly, looses very easily against opponents with common cards. Many people complain over others that have aquired the rarest cards in the game (Legendarys). But the first Master rank I know of (Master is the highest rank in game currently) only played common and rare cards wich are the two lowest card tiers except for regulars that are awarded during the initial level up process. WIth that said. Rare cards does not equal a better card. Tactic and the know-how to counter the opponents card is crucial.
THe single-player campin consist of 3x5 battles I belive and is lack-luster at best. These servers more like a tutorial for the player to learn the game and level-up so that you can get most of the regual cards before you get to online-fightning and raise ones battle-rank. THis is a bit sad since I am a heavy single-player player.
You get one Master at the beginning. Other Masters go through a free-roatiation system that you can play for free at those time. If you want to be sure to always play those Master you have to buy it with the in-game resources. A Master have diffrent attacks and also a perk system. By controlling bridges in the game you get XP that levels up the Master. Up to 4 Perks can be aquired where that fourth and last perk is always Mana frenzy.
All in all I'm happy and surprised how much I enjoy this game. Updates comes regualary and new cards get added with it. New Masters are gonna be added soon. The devs are very communicative and listens to feed-back. Nerfing and buffing is gonna be frequent in teh early stages, but that is to be expected in an EA-game.

After playing this game for a few hours I've managed to make some very basic houses. Sounds boring, yes, but I now know I can never go back to Minecraft and its cube blocks again. Sorry buddy. You will be missed.
The first house I created was ayssemtrical. Every block you place down has that signature Lego clicking sound, so it feels soooo satisfying. So as I was creating my first house I had some choices: Should I use the piece that is 1 peg wide or 2 pegs wide for my foundation? This to me was monumental. Just a simple choice, but a choice that has been lacking for so long in a building game. I went with 1 peg wide to allow me to have more space in my house. Usually with the classic 1meter by 1 meter blocks of Minecraft, it was very difficult to implement any sort of crazy details into the structure. Lego bricks allow you to be much more precise and focus more on the details. On the corners of my house I ended up using the smallest bricks which allowed me to give my house an extremely realistic-looking diagonal shape.
Keep in mind this is all a learning process as well. Since there are a multitude of different bricks available, you are able to focus more on the details of your creations, but at the same time it is very challenging to gain an understanding of even the most basic of building methods. This to me is a PRO, however, because it challenges you to best utilize your equipment to yield the best results. For example: after I was done creating my foundation I moved onto the roof. It took me at least a couple tries to get the roof done right. After a couple of hideous failures, I was finally successful in creating an aesthitcally pleasing and practical roof for my house. Taking what I had learned so far and applying it into my structures was such a joy.
I have many more things to learn before I can build truly masterful creations. That's the appeal of this game for me: more choices and a higher learning curve. You actually have to put time into learning basic methods so you can create even the most basic of structures, and I love it. I have since created a few more houses, and along the way i have been learning new techniques, so each house is looking a bit better than the last.
In minecraft, creations only looked impressive if they were immense in scale as a result of a very limited selection of blocks. Once the community gets a hold of this game, however, creations will not only be immense in scale, but extremely detailed and intricate. I cannot wait to see what the community creates.

Ori and the Blind Forest is a beautiful, modern, and challenging platformer with a heartwarming story. 9/10
Pros:

- Good soundtrack and voice-overs
- Many secrets and power-ups
- Saving is allowed most anywhere
- Feels unique compared with other platformers (similar to Braid)
Cons:
- Several difficult sequences must be played through without saving, which can be frustrating when you die over and over from instakills (and you will).
- Controls are good, but not excellent for three reasons:
1. Sometimes there are multiple ways to perform an action, sometimes only one specific one the game wants you to use, but usually it isn't clear which.
2. Certain actions require a complcated sequence of actions/buttons to perform (e.g. charge-leaping from a wall)
3. Controls feel just slightly imprecise when you need to hit a narrow platform or wall.
Overall highly recommended for any fan of the platformer genre.

This is definitely the best graphic ship game of its kind (sandbox).  The battles on the sea take into account waves, angles, environment, physics, etc... This makes ship control and cannon fire realistic for the time period.
What will make this game successfull:
1) The Devs are doing it right, keep the outpost, teleport and shipping system in place, otherwise the map is too large to make this game playable.  Also, these features support the crafting and economy systems in the game.
2) Provide a variety of missions to keep the game interesting.
3) Long term success means combining PVP and PVE into one sandbox.  The map must be split to support both play styles (PVP and PVE).  In other words, dedicated protected and PVP zones. Both play styles will act to support the economy in the game.
Benefits:
+ Protected zones provide new players a place to play and learn the game.  Also , any player
can  choose pvp, pve or both styles of play at any given time.
+ Both PVP and PVE act to drive the economy and crafting.  PVP and PVE missions will act
to drvie the need for ship buiding, crafting and other aspects of the economy. For sure, PVP
will drive the PVE play for ship building.
+ Combining the best features of PVE (missions, treasures, etc. ) and PVP (hunting, battles and
pirating) into one sandbox means a larger player base which usually means a more exciting
game.

Sproggiwood is a well made charming roguelike with cute graphics and mild RPG elements. While simple on the surface, it boils down to a good amount of tactical complexity.
+Quick download
+Cute, clean & crisp graphics
+Good tutorial
+Great controller support, however, see cons
+Quick n EZ tutorialization
+Good writing
+Good sense of humor
+Fun storyline
-Awkward controller controls (I have a generic though.)
-Some minor bugs sprinkled throughout.
+/-Difficulty scaling/class imbalance might be problematic.
Welcome to Sproggiwood, where you inhabit the island of Cog as a peaceful farmer. One day a talking sheep appears, and obviously you are beholden to it immediately. It tells you to follow it, you do. Monsters appear, you slay them. A mysterious portal appears. You are told to heedlessly waltz through it. You do that as well! Then you discover he is the evil Sproggi! Evil spirit of the realm, and you will do his bidding! What kind of bidding will you do, you wonder?
Sproggiwood is a standard modern rogue-like game with all the bells and whistles that come with them, distilled down to the simplest elements that add back up to tactical complexity. The only thing potentially stopping it from being a true rogue-like would be the permanent progression unlocks earned with gold. Otherwise it's all there. You've got your health, your enemies, your dungeons, your overarcing story, your traps, and a turn-based grid-based floor to slay hordes in.
In Sproggiwood you will, as previously mentioned, unlock permanent upgrades or better gear by getting gold. You get gold by beating dungeons, you get new gear (purchasable) by finding it in dungeons, and you get bonus gold the first time you beat a dungeon with a new class. These upgrades are very important and having the right gear at the right time can save your life. There are also building upgrades that will enable faster exp gains, more health, and more cryptic statues and things of that like.
Most of your adventuring will be the standard roguelike formula of diving into a dungeon and doing your damnedest to survive as long as you can, though. The difficulty curve spikes up well enough, and there's a good amount of enemy variety that forces tactical decision making, all in all Sproggiwood is a solid rogue-like that is simple to learn and only slightly hard to master, but is fun either way.
The graphics in Sproggiwood are great! They're crisp, clean, and colorful. To me, they seem retro-inspired, but like they would fit in well on a tablet. They scale well with resolution so are likely based on vectors graphics. The simplicity gives off a great vibe and allows you to be immersed in the action.
You can see for yourself what they look like pretty clearly. To sum up my opinion on them:
Effective.
The sounds in Sproggiwood are pretty okay, but the music is great. It's upbeat. It's springy. It has mellow guitar and flute and stuff, hooray! There's actually some relatively nice ambient noise in the background as well, if you take the time to notice.
Don't be decieved by the cute graphics, Sproggiwood is a real roguelike with plenty of fun and challenge to be had, and the progression system will keep you moving forward.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine is pretty cool I guess.
Set in the distant future where mankind decided that skulls on everything was totally in. The Imperium of Man has spread thoughout the known galaxy with the guidance of a super powered god-like figure known as the Emperor of Mankind. But the Emperor was betrayed by his favored son, Horus, and after a bloody civil war and the defeat of Horus, the Emperor was left as a crippled body upon a golden throne, which is the only thing that's keeping him alive.
Now 10,000 years later, humanity is beset on all sides by mutants, aliens, and the forces of Chaos.
But it's not all hopeless, for the armies of mankind also have the Space Marines! genetically altered and augmented super soldiers clad in power armor and armed with weapons that would break your arm if you as much as tried to use them. These Space Marines are split into chapters, and no chapter is greater than the Ultramarines, warriors who lead and try to set an example for all Space Marines to follow.
So basically they're the brown-nosing nerds of the 40k Universe.
You play as Titus, a Space Marine captain of the Ultramarines. Which is to say he's the star quarterback on a team made entirely out of quarterbacks. You and your team of similarly jacked super soldiers are deployed on the planet Graia, a Forgeworld that focuses on military development as well as the development of super cool giant robots! Graia is under attack by Orks, a war-like race of fungus based aliens that consist entirely of soccer hooligans that come in sizes ranging from big to Big to BIG. Also little Goblins called Gretchins, but they don't matter.
Titus must secure the giant robot making factory so that the orks don't strip down the giant robot sitting inside for parts. Which would be...Heresy? I think?
Yeah, heresy!
Space Marine is a third person shooter with an emphasis on getting down and dirty with your enemy. Which is sexy, but also not. You are given a plethora of weapons to carry, as well as a choice of melee weapon for when you have to put your arms up at 10 and 2 against the alien scumbags. While your weapons fill most of the essential shooter roles, one stands out the most, which is your standard issue Bolter, which is an assault  weapon that fires .75 calibre rounds which are explosive tipped and rocket propelled.
I don't think understand what I just said. You are essentially firing the fist of an angry at anything dumb enough to not be born human, and sometimes humans as well because screw em.
But sometimes the orks get close and you have to have a strong word with them, and what better way to do that then with a chainsword. A chainsaw sword.
A sword that doubles as a chainsaw.
It's a chainsaw on a stick.
Am I even getting through to you right now?
Not only do you have a Chainsword, but you also have a power axe, a weapon covered in a blue-hazy force field THAT IS CAPABLE OF DISRUPTING THE MOLECULAR BONDS OF MATTER WHEN IT STRIKES
And a thunder hammer, a giant hammer... Also it explodes.
How the game works is that you mix your two styles of combat together, engaging your enemies from a distance with your ranged weapons and then closing in with your melee weapon to give them a stern talking to.
And by that I mean murder.
Your enemies will always outnumber you, so 9 times out of 10 you're going to be in melee combat anyway. The melee itself isn't all that impressive, you have an attack button and you have a stun button, but you can also grab stunned enemies and turn them into a fine red paste for health. That's the only way you can get your health back, you execute the stunned enemies in a gory fashion which refills your health like you're some sort of buff vampire.
Or you can get really mad  for a few seconds and let your health refill that way.
Luckily, the weapons in this game are crunchy enough to feel rewarding for every playstyle so don't be afraid to mix it up. You're going to get into melee combat, either way. So at least the weapons feel nice to use.
Titus himself, as a Space Marine, is a pretty heavy fellow, but don't say that to his face because you might hurt his feelings, and Titus is a nice guy. You monster.
Oh yeah, also he can kill you.
The Space Marines move with weighted thuds to every one of their steps, making them seem like lumbering oafs at first, until you get Titus to go into a charge. Now he's like a rip roaring retard rhino that can smash down everything in his way. Space Marines are surprisingly agile for their size, but I guess that comes with the whole Super Soldier thing. You'd think that at least their pauldrons get in the way, but they don't seem to have a problem with them.

Superficially one can look at Downwell and jusst see a cheap game, but while it's cheap Downwell does what it's proposes to do in a primorous way. At the first sight the gameplay is basic and simple, you have a button to jump/shoot from your boots and can move left and right, and while the controls are indeed simple there are more nuances to it, like a wall jump you can do, maintaining a combo to gain it's bonuses once you finish it or choosing the best upgrades to fit the style you choose to play.
In my modest opinion Downwell shines in the small details, like after reaching a new "world" the music only starts after you land on a platform or in an enemy. Using a limited color palette but still makes it easy to distinguish between the enemies you can land on from the ones you need to avoid to not take damage, and the same applies to environment and as you progress through the game you unlock more colors. Other small thing I appreciate in the game is since the time pauses when you enter one of the side rooms the music stops, and you not loses your combo, even though you recharge your boots by landing on them.
I short i highly recommend this game.

The Warhammer setting and mechanics however totally convinced me. I have spent >100 hours on Warhammer I and pre ordered Warhammer II and never regretted it to this day.

This is an excellent game. For strategy lovers, fans of Warhammer, players of Total War games, and people who enjoy micromanagement with real time battles and good looks.
I played almost all Total War titles since the fist Shogun, and I love the brand, but immersion differed between titles.
I will compare Warhammer II with other titles of the series, and it's predecessor, Warhammer I. For people who never played Total War titles before: This is an in depth, complex strategy game, that, like other games of this stature take some time to adjust to and master. But once you get the hang of it, it shines as very unique and rich in it's category.
- Both the campaign and Mortal Empire maps look good and offer interesting start positions and campaign decisions.
- You have a choice between a rather short victory path through the Vortex mechanic, or a very long victory path through the Domination one. That last one will go into 300+ turns easily.
- Characters can become immortal, meaning that you never permanently loose them, which is a nice tweak.
- Characters can gain positive and negative traits far more transparent and through a more diverse array of actions, which  adds nicely to talents and gear
- The four different races have very, very disinct playstyles, with some highly interesting mechanics that set them apart. Unit rosters seem balanced and also quite differentiated, with some leaning more to melee, others to ranged or heavy units.
- Agents are more useful than ever, be it as part of an army and boosting things like replenishment, be it solo on the campaign map where they really can set the odds in your favor at times.
- Very nice are the random sea encounters where you can find items and pretty sunbstantial amounts of gold. The same holds for the dilemma's encountered when you search ruins.
- The battle maps are hand designed and offer some variety in tactics, like huge forests, hillpositions, and bottlenecks.
- In most TW games trade was rather superficial, often meaning that you had excess of almost any resource without any use. Now you can gain serious ecenomic income from trade, and getting resources becomes a strategic importance.
- This, together with some additional benefits that resouces bring, like reduced upkeep for special troops, and the many unique building chains that some regions offer make for far more interesting campaign choices, and a lively difference between regions. Conquering lands is less generic and grindy because of this, and more satisfying.
- The most important thing for me in strategy games is how well the AI presents a challenge, especially when your empire grows in strength. This is where some TW titles failed, as your growing empire was never matched with equally stong competitors. This is absolutely great in TW Warhammer II, better than any title so far. I only played Very Hard and Legendary, and rival factions expand tremendously, offering very tough challenges, and fielding very elite armies. This means that the tension of the the first 50 turns is carried on almost towards the end game, and I cannot stress enough how important this is in a strategy game.
- All in all this games shines in rewarding the player with encounters, gear, unique regions, special units, the unlocking of technology, and much more. That, in combination with an ongoing challenge throughout the game (at least on higher difficulties), means that the immersion and tension span are very well implemented. On par or better than the best TW titles.
- The only drawbacks are that the domination victory still can become a bit of a grind towards the end, but any strategy game knows a point after which winning is just a formality.

Early Access V 0.9.1
Before we start I got a game key for free during alpha but since Early access I bought the premium upgrade at the same price as all new players since early access launch because currently premium upgrade includes in all new purchases.
The game revolves in the Forced universe. Betadwarf has made two prior games, Forced and Forced Showdown. I have played extensivly Forced Showdown and had alot of fun with it. WIth that in mind I had very high hopes for betadwarfs third game, Minion Masters.
Minion Masters is the PC-variant of Clash Royale were players aquire cards (minions, spells, buildings) and put togethor a deck of 8 cards and battle an random opponent. The goal is to lower the health of the opponents master by 3000 points.
(V.S friend battle is in development).
Tactics and counter knowledge is crucial to be a winner. All new players gets rubies, shards and gold because of the premium upgrade. Rubies are an purchable in-game currency (it is also rewarded by leveling up at certain levels and raise in leauge rank). Shards are also rewarded in the same regard as rubies, but are not purchable and can also be aquired if by spinning the power tower wheel (it is where you spend gold to get a random card). If you get a dublicate card, it is salvaged and you get shards in relation of that cards rarity.
The game is still in beta and under heavy development and balancing. Some cards might be a bit OP. But players with OP cards that plays badly, looses very easily against opponents with common cards. Many people complain over others that have aquired the rarest cards in the game (Legendarys). But the first Master rank I know of (Master is the highest rank in game currently) only played common and rare cards wich are the two lowest card tiers except for regulars that are awarded during the initial level up process. WIth that said. Rare cards does not equal a better card. Tactic and the know-how to counter the opponents card is crucial.
THe single-player campin consist of 3x5 battles I belive and is lack-luster at best. These servers more like a tutorial for the player to learn the game and level-up so that you can get most of the regual cards before you get to online-fightning and raise ones battle-rank. THis is a bit sad since I am a heavy single-player player.
You get one Master at the beginning. Other Masters go through a free-roatiation system that you can play for free at those time. If you want to be sure to always play those Master you have to buy it with the in-game resources. A Master have diffrent attacks and also a perk system. By controlling bridges in the game you get XP that levels up the Master. Up to 4 Perks can be aquired where that fourth and last perk is always Mana frenzy.
All in all I'm happy and surprised how much I enjoy this game. Updates comes regualary and new cards get added with it. New Masters are gonna be added soon. The devs are very communicative and listens to feed-back. Nerfing and buffing is gonna be frequent in teh early stages, but that is to be expected in an EA-game.
Graphics 9/10
GAmeplay 8/10
FUn-factor 9/10
(A tip to new players: Before you spend all your rubies and shards. Read forum and play a couple of battles and ask for tips. THat way you gonna know wich cards to craft and what tactic to use. This gonna reduce alot of frustrations early on before you can get most of the cards)

"There's a place you just can't reach unless you have a dream too large to bear alone. We call everything on the ice 'love.'"
I've seen this anime before when it came out late 2016, and I was so surprised to come across it again on steam. I decided to buy the entire season (thank God it wasn't expensive as some other anime shows are on here) and binge watched it within two days.
PROS (*may contain spoilers*):
1.) Yuri on Ice has a simple plot where you have the main character, Yuri Katsuki, struggling at first not only with ice skating, but with himself. After a rough season, Yuri decides to take a "break" from ice skating and heads back to his hometown in Japan. Back at his old ice rink, he performs a routine by the champion of ice skating himself, Victor Nikiforov. Impressed by Katsuki's performance of his own routine, Victor decides to take a trip down to Japan and you can guess what happens next. I love this series where you can watch Yuri's character growth progress with the help of Nikiforov and other characters. You see people being pushed to their limits aiming towards one main goal- winning gold at the Grand Prix. I also enjoyed how it felt like you were part of the experience and actually watching the ice skating competitions itself. It keeps you on edge of your seat a lot of the time where you are cheering on your favorite character to win. This series doesn't solely focus inside the ice rink, but life outside the rink as well. Yuri on Ice also touches upon anxiety. This series had me on a roller coaster of emotions where i was crying in one scene, but laughing in the next. Either way, this series can honestly be enjoyed by everybody and you can be able to get something out of it.
2.) Diverse cast of such loveable characters (but not to the point where it's a whole lot). You have characters from all over the world of different ages. They even hint at some real skaters and have a few professional ice skaters come  voice in the show! The show features some well-known Japanese voice actors, such as: Toshiyuki Toyonaga (feat. in Durarara!! and Tokyo Ghoul), Junichi Suwabe (feat. in Black Butler and Space Dandy), Hiroki Yasumoto (feat. in Hetalia and Fairy Tail), and Mamoru Miyano (feat. in Death Note and Ouran High School Host Club).
3.) *MY FAVORITE* The music in this show is absolutely phenomenal!! From "History Maker" to "The King and the Skater" to "Theme of King JJ" to "Stay Close to Me," the music was very diverse and just perfectly fits the show and characters so well.
4.) Honestly, the fanservice in this anime wasn't bad. I know when i started watching this anime before last year, i was constantly worried about how much fanservice there wpuld be like in "Diabolik Lovers" or "Brother's Conflict." This series still had some  fanservice but still stuck to its plot as well. They didn't overdo it.
5.) The artstyle in this anime wasn't bad most of the time, but it wasn't the best in a few scenes. You saw beautiful scenes on the beach or looking over the city/town with astonishing colors. The designs and costumes of the characters were absolutely amazing.
6.) I really enjoyed how there were short information segments on ice skating in the anime. Obviously, there will be some viewers who may never have watched an actual ice skating competition before (like me) and will have no clue on how the sport is scored, who gets into the final, etc. These segments had cute little  drawings with them as well.
CON(S):
1.) Like I said, artstyle wasn't too bad but wasn't the best in a few scenes (like some of the characters looked weird in some shots.) The show still makes up in other ways though so it's all good.
2.) I felt like this series could've been longer and I wish it was. The series contains 12 episodes that you can easily watch within a day if you wanted too. I think they could've done more episodes where they focused on character backgrounds and stories, especially with some of the supporting characters.
3.)  On steam, you can only buy it in its original japanese form with english subtitles. I watched both japanese and english dubs, and was kind of sad they didn't add the english dub as an option on steam. Overall, I'm still pretty happy Yuri on Ice was added xD
I totally recommend watching this series. Most people that I recommended it (and who have watched it) enjoyed the show so much. SEE YOU NEXT LEVEL! <3

After playing this game for a few hours I've managed to make some very basic houses. Sounds boring, yes, but I now know I can never go back to Minecraft and its cube blocks again. Sorry buddy. You will be missed.
The first house I created was ayssemtrical. Every block you place down has that signature Lego clicking sound, so it feels soooo satisfying. So as I was creating my first house I had some choices: Should I use the piece that is 1 peg wide or 2 pegs wide for my foundation? This to me was monumental. Just a simple choice, but a choice that has been lacking for so long in a building game. I went with 1 peg wide to allow me to have more space in my house. Usually with the classic 1meter by 1 meter blocks of Minecraft, it was very difficult to implement any sort of crazy details into the structure. Lego bricks allow you to be much more precise and focus more on the details. On the corners of my house I ended up using the smallest bricks which allowed me to give my house an extremely realistic-looking diagonal shape.
Keep in mind this is all a learning process as well. Since there are a multitude of different bricks available, you are able to focus more on the details of your creations, but at the same time it is very challenging to gain an understanding of even the most basic of building methods. This to me is a PRO, however, because it challenges you to best utilize your equipment to yield the best results. For example: after I was done creating my foundation I moved onto the roof. It took me at least a couple tries to get the roof done right. After a couple of hideous failures, I was finally successful in creating an aesthitcally pleasing and practical roof for my house. Taking what I had learned so far and applying it into my structures was such a joy.
I have many more things to learn before I can build truly masterful creations. That's the appeal of this game for me: more choices and a higher learning curve. You actually have to put time into learning basic methods so you can create even the most basic of structures, and I love it. I have since created a few more houses, and along the way i have been learning new techniques, so each house is looking a bit better than the last.
In minecraft, creations only looked impressive if they were immense in scale as a result of a very limited selection of blocks. Once the community gets a hold of this game, however, creations will not only be immense in scale, but extremely detailed and intricate. I cannot wait to see what the community creates.

After clearing 4 files in a row since I purchased it without picking up another game inbetween playthroughs, I can tell you without a shadow of a doubt that this game is incredible. This game reminded me precisely what I loved so much about the 2d exploration games of the SNES era, most notably Super Metroid. And although it's very much like Metroid in an exploration sense of finding where the items you need to progress are, it's also very much it's own game given it's extreme emphasis on platforming that those exploration games never had. Getting from place to place is challenging, but rewarding. After clearing a temple, the chaos that ensues is exhilarating! During these parts, it's forcing you to learn how to utilize the powerup you earned to near perfection in order to make it out alive, which will ensure that you know precisely how to control Ori when you're just out in the world. Which is where even more of the fun comes. When I say "platforming" don't mistake what I say as this being just a "jump here, jump there" kind of game. You don't simply jump when you get to the edge of a platform in order to get where you need to go. It's more like "double jump here, wall jump off that, bash off that enemy, bash off that projectile, rocket jump off the wall, etc." There are so many options for maneuverability that it makes it far more entertaining to get around in Ori than it was in other platformers before it. Just getting around is fun, especially since the world itself is so beautiful.
There are only a few minor flaws:
First of all, if you like to complete games 100%. Make sure you do everything in the temples before you leave. You can not re-enter a cleared temple. And second of all once you beat the game you CAN NOT play a cleared file. So if you want to keep playing, you have to start from the beginning if you actually completed the game.
The only other problem is something I imagine will get patched, but basically the screen, at random intervals, flips upside  down during every cutscene. It's annoying, but doesn't make the game unplayable or unenjoyable. I would just like to see the cutscenes how they were supposed to be portrayed.
EDIT: This issue has been fixed
But flaws aside, again this game is absolutely wonderful. This is the game that will keep you from playing other games, because you just won't want to put it down. And the great part is that you won't even feel bad about it. It's just that much fun.
We need more games like this. Incredible.

Vero e proprio capolavoro.
Un GDR con combattimento a turni con un gameplay veramente di altissimo livello: eccelso sistema di combattimento, probabilmente, per ora, il migliore in circolazione, (con tanto di sfruttamento degli elementi che possono influenzare l'ambiente in svariati modi), ottima interazione ambientale (funzionale ai bisogni del giocatori), buona IA degli avversari, e la presenza della modalità coperativa, per giocare la campagna insieme ad un'altra persona. Il gioco difatti è sviluppato sopratutto per questa modalità, offrendo un'esperienza inedita, più che innovativa per questo genere. Inoltre, il mondo di gioco è completamente esplorabile, offrendo un'esperienza dalle sfumature "openworld", dove effettivamente si ha la completa libertà di interagire con ogni oggetto o PNG, compreso uccidere chiunque si voglia, senza compromettere il completamento del gioco. Anche la trama, nella sua semplicità e secondarietà, è carina.
Gli unici difetti sono la mancanza di possibilità di compiere scelte serie nei dialoghi (fondamentali per un'esperienza ruolistica soddisfacente), un certo sbilanciamento tra le varie "classi" (rami di abilità più che altro), e la casualità del drop degli items.
Ma complessivamente risulta essere probabilmente uno dei migliori titoli GDR di sempre. Assolutamente da provare.

"Hey, what's this? A L4D2 copy?"
Well, not really. Codename cure is a source based ga- or just read the description.
My thoughts on this game:
It does have elements inspired by L4D2, hell. It used the source engine! But inspiration doesn't mean a full on copy. (Also this game seems more similar to Killing floor or such, not too sure but oh well.) Generally this game is enjoyable and while it feels wonky the gameplay and entertainment it has makes up for the bullets. (I still don't know how they do hitscan.)
Gameplay itself:
Rather enjoyable and a mix between defense and offense for the classes. Just because they have one class that's perfect for holding a choke point doesn't mean the other can't do it.
Take the pointman for example, spam all of his shots down a choke and the zombies will struggle to pass, or mow them all down by blasting them in the face. (Results may vary.)
Or the Sniper, his hipfire is great for close combat and his pistol provides even more support whenever you're getting pressured by the zombos. (Or punch them in the face, because a human fist is totally more powerful than a 7.72mm sniper rifle shot. Totally.)
Oh, there's also skins, just like CS:GO, only it's co-op and all you kill are zombies.
I could ramble on but I'll keep it short. I like it, simple yet pleasing (Especially the physics.)
Gameplay mechanics:
Ok, this is where I have questions, it works well but visually seems weird? You will be able to see the bullet travel but a click will have bloodsplats or bullet holes directly where you aimed, sometimes without the bullet viewmodel even travelling. This makes it rather hard to determine whether or not you hit a zombie so relying on a bloodsplat or bullet hole is key. (Unless I'm doing something wrong.)
The rest of the functions seem slow or undesireable, especially in this game. Such as when you're trying to pick up a sentry gun but fail and see it explode in front of your face and cry about it since you can't get another sentry gun unless you respawn. (Sad life) but that's what add to the action. Making a misclick and ruining a essential item is what gives you a "Don't rush the functions but be quick" mentality. (last time I checked supply chests were invincible, but I think they gave it a health bar too.)
Or just chuck grenades, you can damage yourself in the process to help with sacrifice!
Also melee, it feels rather accurate and the pixel hitbox for it relies on your distance and where you're aiming. But it again also feels a little weird, like times when you fist a zombie only to punch the air due to bad registration (Even though you actually punched the zombie.) But it's a rather stable mechanic and you won't find yourself being frusturated by it.
Movement:
"Oh boi, time to go speedy and zoom zoom past all these zom zoms!" - Xx_sp33d_runn3r42069_xX
Sorry, but zombies limit your movement little boy.
"But but, zoom zooms are needed for me to run like sanic!"
Try strafing, or backpedalling, or you know. Not rely on sprint like in Call of Duty.
The movement is slightly faster than the runners, but that doesn't mean you can just bypass them like some other game such as PayDay or something else, strafing and other forms of movement are required to keep your feet moving. Especially if you're getting by a horde of them, and a horde of them comes with at least 30 zom zoms.
Keep in mind that 30 zom zoms are not a low number, and that's the lowest amount.
A.I.:
I'd have to say they function similarly to the Payday 2 A.I. because they follow the character and shoot the cop- I mean zombies, they can also use their special functions but I'm not too sure on the support A.I. (Because I always play support or Technician, Pointman and Assault mains hmu.)
Zombie A.I. is rather simple; Chase down the player, but don't let that get to you since the zombies can appear from unexpected places and you wouldn't even know that while being chased by 10 other zombies. So even with simple A.I. they can still provide a challenge, unless they're acting dumb and rambling around. (That is until they notice you like a Japanese school anime character.)
Zombie types:
Just 3 zombies categories and 3 attacks.
Zombies:
fast: Zoom zoom, gonna zom zom your booty
normal: Running zombies in 2017? Pssh, that's so 2015
heavy: Hey, I'll take all your bullets and destroy your health and armor! Wait, what happened to my legs?
rapid: Basically arms flailing and poor damage, this will kill your speed so badly.
medium: Just a normal swipe, not too hard to escape.
hard: Might as well just die from your own grenade if you're hit by these like multiple times.
(The heavy zombies only have the hard attack, the other zombies vary and can be random at times. But generally the fast zombies have the rapid attack.)
Game balance:
The ratings definitely fit, unless you're playing with A.I. but it's still rather fitting even with A.I. (Since they can actually die! Woah!)
The difficulty do match their words. This is an example of those words.
Normal: Woah, I have lots of ammo, zombies barely do damage, they also don't come at me like a damn zombie apocalypse inside of an apartment building.
Hard: Less ammo? Okay. More damage from zombies? Okay. Swarms of zombies? Okay.
Insane: Where's the ammo box at? Why am I so low on health? Why is there literally a couple dozen zombies chasing me while my team is dead? Why am I about to die?
Servers:
I play custom only, can't judge what I can't do.
Overall, I love this game and it being free is rather surprising considering how fun it is.

After clearing 4 files in a row since I purchased it without picking up another game inbetween playthroughs, I can tell you without a shadow of a doubt that this game is incredible. This game reminded me precisely what I loved so much about the 2d exploration games of the SNES era, most notably Super Metroid. And although it's very much like Metroid in an exploration sense of finding where the items you need to progress are, it's also very much it's own game given it's extreme emphasis on platforming that those exploration games never had. Getting from place to place is challenging, but rewarding. After clearing a temple, the chaos that ensues is exhilarating! During these parts, it's forcing you to learn how to utilize the powerup you earned to near perfection in order to make it out alive, which will ensure that you know precisely how to control Ori when you're just out in the world. Which is where even more of the fun comes. When I say "platforming" don't mistake what I say as this being just a "jump here, jump there" kind of game. You don't simply jump when you get to the edge of a platform in order to get where you need to go. It's more like "double jump here, wall jump off that, bash off that enemy, bash off that projectile, rocket jump off the wall, etc." There are so many options for maneuverability that it makes it far more entertaining to get around in Ori than it was in other platformers before it. Just getting around is fun, especially since the world itself is so beautiful.
There are only a few minor flaws:
First of all, if you like to complete games 100%. Make sure you do everything in the temples before you leave. You can not re-enter a cleared temple. And second of all once you beat the game you CAN NOT play a cleared file. So if you want to keep playing, you have to start from the beginning if you actually completed the game.
The only other problem is something I imagine will get patched, but basically the screen, at random intervals, flips upside  down during every cutscene. It's annoying, but doesn't make the game unplayable or unenjoyable. I would just like to see the cutscenes how they were supposed to be portrayed.
EDIT: This issue has been fixed
But flaws aside, again this game is absolutely wonderful. This is the game that will keep you from playing other games, because you just won't want to put it down. And the great part is that you won't even feel bad about it. It's just that much fun.
We need more games like this. Incredible.

Ori and the Blind Forest is a beautiful game. Its graphical/art style is gorgeous and unique, and the soundtrack is totally emotional and incredible. This game gives me a lot of the same kind of vibes as from watching Studio Ghibli films like Spirited Away or Princess Mononoke. OatBF's aesthetic isn't the only thing that's beautiful; the story working in-tandum with the colourful visuals and haunting music is what makes this game great. There is virtually no dialogue; the story is told through sporadic narration and character's movements and emotions. It really is quite an achievement that this kind of storytelling can invoke such emotional feelings (tears within the first 10 minutes).
Gameplay-wise, it's okay. I haven't played platform games since my early days of playing Rayman and Super Mario, but I did enjoy the simple yet progressively complex gameplay in this. As you unlock new abilities you can traverse the Forest of Nibel in increasingly diverse ways, and this game has the usual platform game tropes of hidden areas or areas to return to once you have the appropriate abilities. This game is surprisingly difficult towards after the first half of the story; the trial and error style gameplay did get me frustrated - I died, a lot - and I'll admit that towards the end I just wanted to finish and get to the ending.
Gameplay faults, however, are largely irrelevant because it is OatBF's aforementioned story/aesthetic is what makes this game worth playing. I was really impressed and I am now considering buying Moon Studios' other titles, Journey and Flower, as well as buying this game's soundtrack. I'd recommend getting this game even at full price if you're that keen, but if you're apprehensive I'd totally recommend getting it on a sale.

Maybe I'm a victim of the overwhelming hype of the game, but, I did not cry. And, I did not find it to be amazing as I was led to believe. That being said, you are much better off not reading anything about this game and playing it with very little knowledge as to what other's think! Seriously, stop here. Don't let others bias your opinion before you even play.
I encourage you to play the game, though the price (in my opinion) is a bit steap for what it is. So go play it at a friend's house who already has it- especially since it can be finished in a few hours.
The story concept is abosulety great, and would do well as a book or even a short movie. But unfortunately a "game" was made instead. A couple puzzles and the weird "wack-a-mole" thing does not a game make. If it had only been that the controls are extremely clunky, then I could easily over look that- but the story also felt lacking and a bit scatter-brained at times. The creator did well to be subtle with story elements, but did not offer the same consideration to the game play as the puzzles were too easy and became an annoying reoccurance. Not to mention the lack of reset or undo, despite having the possible number of moves and moves you've made being conveyed. (Maybe you can obtain an achievement for this? But in game, this seems to have no importance, and I'm confused to why it was even kept.) The seek-and-find aspect of each level became tedious, and a loss opportunity for multiple hidden objects in a level in which different combinations of objects led you to different levels. That being said, the game is extremely linear and offers absolutely no replay value. Towards the end of the first act I ran across a game breaking bug which required googling. Fortunately I found a forum where a dev responded with an asinine solution. Had I lost my saved file, I would not have restarted due to the slow and clunky controls. I do not need to be reminded every five minutes that you can click to move, though it would've been nice to know that I could walk with the arrows keys from the get go.
The humour is great and had me laughing out loud quite a few times, but it has no place in this game (at least not in its frequency). For a game that's supposed to be heart wrenching, comedy elements shouldn't be sprinkled throughout. I found other additions to the story (like the kids) to be unnecessary.
Also, there's no setting's menu.
That been said, the music and sounds are amazing! Without, the game would have been largely unplayable.
It's a nice game to play on a rainy day if you already have it in your library. And since I feel like one of few who share this opinion, you'll probably love it and it'll make you cry.

This is an awesome game! As a landlubber who grew up 2,000 miles from the closest ocean but loved reading Moby♥♥♥♥♥♥ the Patrick O'Brian novels, and other books about the age of sailing ships, I have longed to go to sea on such a majestic vessel.  Now Naval Action gives me the chance.  The various ships are meticulously rendered, the ocean views at various times of day spectacular, the challenges of managing sails to get the most out of the wind, gunnery choices, and a vast, vast world to explore---they are all here.  The learning curve is steep.  It is difficult to find answers to questions in one source--but for the most part other players are quick to answer Help questions and give advice.  As always, there are things that I wish could be better---though weather sometimes changes, there are no foggy days; wind direction changes but wind speed never does; graphics for boarding and melee is lacking (you make choices on a menu screen and watch changing numbers with a background of an empty deck)--but these are minor quibbles, and some of this may yet still be in the works as this is stil in play test.  But even as is, it is a great adventure!

Superficially one can look at Downwell and jusst see a cheap game, but while it's cheap Downwell does what it's proposes to do in a primorous way. At the first sight the gameplay is basic and simple, you have a button to jump/shoot from your boots and can move left and right, and while the controls are indeed simple there are more nuances to it, like a wall jump you can do, maintaining a combo to gain it's bonuses once you finish it or choosing the best upgrades to fit the style you choose to play.
In my modest opinion Downwell shines in the small details, like after reaching a new "world" the music only starts after you land on a platform or in an enemy. Using a limited color palette but still makes it easy to distinguish between the enemies you can land on from the ones you need to avoid to not take damage, and the same applies to environment and as you progress through the game you unlock more colors. Other small thing I appreciate in the game is since the time pauses when you enter one of the side rooms the music stops, and you not loses your combo, even though you recharge your boots by landing on them.
I short i highly recommend this game.

The art style is really pretty and reminiscent of older point-n-click adventure games like The Dig or Loom, maybe with a little Out of This World thrown in.  It's not as cartoony as other games of the time like Monkey Island or Day of the Tentacle.  The controls are a little weird and there are a lot of musical undertones connecting everything together which is what makes this game fresh.  Couple that with odd pseudo-intellectual psychobabble storytelling and the game does a nice job of holding one's interest, if only from the mystery.
If I had to say anything negative, the controls are a bit...  counter-intuitive, and take awhile to learn but until then I found myself (and still do at times) randomly doing things with the mouse before I end up making what I want happen.  The action is rather minimalistic and a bit disjointed from the rest of the game, but it still remains fun, if not challenging at times.  Most of the game is along the lines of an interactive story, so the combat is kind of neat, not really seen in a point-n-click game like this before.
As for the storytelling, I'm not sure what to say about it, other than I'm still on the fence.  The authors either wrote it to be extremely pretentious and artsy; or it's so convoluted with large vocabulary on purpose as to be an ironic means of giving the player little information while trying to remain vague and mysterious.  If it's the former, I'd rather not have any dialogue, because why say it when you can show it?  If it's the latter, they constantly break this rule by changing the writing style to be as blunt and directly open as possible at times, so you almost end up realizing that when small words are used it might be a real hint and you should pay some attention.  It makes the game come across like there are two or even three writers competing with each other as to how the game flows.  I think with just a little more work they could have done the entire game with no dialogue whatsoever, because the backgrounds, things, and musical sounds throughout the game change depending on what you're doing to them.
Then there's a weird "feature" where the game wants to tweet on your behalf to twitter.  I read that there's no point to this, so I guess it's just a blatant way of hyping up the game, which is kind of interesting, but if there's no reward then why do it?
If you liked older point-n-click adventure games or used to slobber over everything Lucasarts, Tim Schafer, or Ron Gilbert pumped out in the '90s you'll enjoy this game.  It doesn't feel stale and it really does a great job of making you believe the world of the game exists, and you find yourself wondering how neat it would be to actually be there, wandering around exploring.

The basic gameplay of Scribblenauts is solving little puzzles by creating objects that you can then use to manipulate the world. Most of the puzzles are very straightforward, and allow the player to come up with many different solutions, but every now and then I would get stuck on something. Usually it was because the answer the game was looking for was something completely different than I was thinking, so it was unable to interpret how the objects I created were supposed to be a solution. So while the game is pretty smart considering you can input thousands of words, sometimes it just balks and has no idea what you're trying to do.
That said, it's still amazingly fun. There is a map where you can select different levels, each of which you can explore. Each zone has a funny theme, named with a funny grammar pun. The characters that you have to help are often silly and almost always endearing.
Steam achievements: Half of them are completed by being a completionist and making sure you finish every detail in every level. But then the other half of the achievements... don't seem to be listed anywhere. I had to go online to figure out what "find all the object shards" entailed. It was basically a list of special word combinations, and if you spawned them together, or made the items interact with each other, then it counted toward the total score. For instance, one required you to make a marionette with the adjective "alive" to get the "Pinocchio" object shard. How in the world are you supposed to figure that out on your own? I needed a guide to figure out what I was looking for, but I didn't want to just run down a cheat sheet, so I searched for a guide that was simply a list of the object shards without the solutions. That was extremely helpful to get the achievements without feeling like a complete cheater. I looked and could not find a list like this anywhere within the game itself. If there is one in the game, it was pretty darn hidden, which is frustrating.
(Also, the game says you cannot type in proper nouns. However, one of the object shards requires you to create "William Shakespeare". The last time I checked, that was a proper noun. What? Okay, whatever.)
Object editor: So much fun! I didn't do much editing myself, what with my limited artistic skills. But when I found an avatar with 3D glasses, I dyed all of his clothes brown (except for the shoes, of course) and ran around the game, going, "Woooo, I'm the Doctor!"
You can also search for and download other objects that people have created. I downloaded a bunch of Doctor Who objects. I was amazed at the amount of customization people were able to put into the objects, from a piece of celery inside of the TARDIS, to a banana in 9's hand, to the combatitiveness of a dalek. I had a great amount of fun playing with these items that other people had created with the object editor.

I have played Pillars of Eternity, which I kinda enjoyed, and then Tyranny.
I will compare my experience with these two games.
After playing this for a few hours, I can say, I am far more enjoying Divinity Original sin than Obisidian games. Dont get me wrong, their games are amazing, with amazing writing and story, but this game has taken me by something else.
Pros:
- First of all, combat is so much better in this game, holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ I though turn based combat would be horribly boring, like some civilization, but no, it turned out to be best thing they could put into game.
In Pillars or Tyranny, when I didnt won fight the first fight, or died to a boss, I knew I wouldnt beat him the second time.
But here, its like Vanilla wow, you just have to try, new strategy, positioning, using spells wisely, etc.
There was one boss that took more than 7 tries to beat him, which lasted about hourr of real time, but then the sense of achievement when I killed him, man, like in Dark Souls.....
- I LOVE THE VOICE ACTING! :D
Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥some voices are so funny! xD Animals have amazing voice acting, I just sometimes laugh when some creature or zombie talks, its so well acted....
- environment interaction is just taking my breath. You can move objects to disarm traps, conjure rain to extinquish fire, teleport items around, telekinesis, or create cloud near character so he doesnt see you stealing through it, amazing, so much possibilities.
- difficulty is sometimes extreme. With leveling it felt like in Vanilla wow, where you had to do every quest or interaction so you can get the level to not get killed when you get out of time. This proved extremely challenging, which finally kept me interested in the game. I just wasnt on fast train rishing everything with kid difficulty like in so many games these days.
Boss battles were amazing. There was one boss, which summoned several minibosses you had to fight in previous parts of game, which they alone were pretty hard. So when the main boss summoned them, I was like, no way, my journey ends here. Then I died several times trying to beat that boss. When I beat him after an ~hour of fight, I felt such an acommplishement, so good feeling....
- amazing graphics, oviously
- good, simple, straight forward story. The history in Pillars of Eternity was extremely deep and I was lost in it after few hours of playing, too much knowledge was thrown at you during gameplay.
Cons:
- my only con was crafting. I discovered it after several hours of gameplay and even now I dont very much use it, its not very simple and its very hard to craft armor or weapons, you either wont have materials or will have to search internet for crafting combinations
- the conversation fight, rock, paper, sissors is just horrible. There is no skill involved, compete RNG, and it sometimes decides whether you can completele quest or not, or whether the guy you are talking to will kill you if RNG doesnt favor you.....
Anyway, this game is 9/10 for me, certainly one of best RPGs I have ever playd (have not even finished it yet), and I cannot wait to play Divinity Original Sin 2 when it comes out of Early Access!

I will start things of by saying: I was never much of a Jump&Run (or platformer or whatever you want to call it) player. I liked some of them in the 90s (Lion King!) but eventually, they got to a difficulty, it was just annoying to keep on playing. On the other hand, I find games that are too easy (like COD, with their Autohealing) boring.
Recently some of those games popped up again - like the Trine series - that got my interest into that genre back, so I tried Ori.
Ori is none of the above:while  it is challenging (and therefore NOT boring) from the beginning, it never gets to a point where you want to stop playing. Because once you master the challenging situation, you get a new ability, with that the gameplay changes and feels more and more rewarding.
Although there are situations where you will die 20 or 30 times, and want to throw your controller (or keyboard) into the corner, the game is too beatiful (graphics but also design in general, sound, story, gameplay) to be stopped playing.
Several things in that great are so well thought through, that you can only imagine how much love and work went into it.
I am not talking about the (in other reviews) many times mentioned graphics or the great soundtrack, I am talking about how perfect the level design is:
The whole world could be described as an "Open World" design, but you cannot attempt every location at first. With every ability you learn, you get access to new parts and paths. While this seems annoying by description, you don't see these new paths - until you learn the new ability (like a higher jump or so).
Later, when you stop by at the level you have run through several times, it always feels new and rewarding, because you can unlock secrets and even better abilities by going back and checking for some new paths.
It's amazing how every piece of the world has to be designed for every possible ability "Ori" can have.
And there is such a high variety in the game. Every level/world feels different, has different gameplay and challenges. So do the opponents. And the story is heartwarming as well. Its not black and white (good guy vs bad guy), but the characters are somewhat deep and have all good and bad parts in it.
Even with the Witcher 3 out, so far this is the biggest surprise 2015 and until this point my game of the year.
Because it's been a while since I've been so amazed by a game (Doom, 1993, Half Life 98, STALKER 2007 and DX:HR in 2011), this is my first review ever here on Steam (and propably the only one) I wrote.
So in the end I would rate that game 9/10, but only because 10/10 is the "perfect" game, which is not possible by definition... also because there has to be room for improvement. Or a part 2, which I hope will be in the making by now.
