This game is amazing. For me, it is the fufillment of a childhood dream; to be a captian on the high seas, sailing the ships that I constantly drew and studied as a child. This effect was tripled when the Devs added the wonderful USS Essex into the game; I've been drawing that ship since I was in 1st grade. Thanks devs, for helping me fufill a long-thought dream.
I'll plainly lay out pros/cons for your convenience, dear reader.
+The game's open world is amazing! The map is massive, filled with beautiful islands and ports- and enemies too. It's breathakingly beautiful.
+Ship models are mind-blowing not only in beauty, but accuracy.  You're not sailing a digital representation in low def; you're sailing an exact recreation of the real thing. Perhaps not as "rugged" as people imagine, but beautiful nevertheless.
+Ship performance and customization systems are extremley detailed and advanced! Characteristics of a ship range heavily from turn rate, speed and even the thickness of your hull- much more involved. A pantheon of upgrades allows you to customize your own ship to fit your play style, which is incredible.
+Combat system is divine. The game's entire purpose is first as an age of sail combat simulator, and they nailed it here. Ships perform accuratley as they would in real life; spare for a 25% speed boost from the real thing. Perform complex manuavers like tacking, box hauling, etc, outsmart your enemy in so many ways.
+Ballistics engine is mind-blowing. There's no "hp bar"; shots can penetrate through hull, create splinters that could kill some crew standing by a gun, bounce around the other side of the hull (or exit), carry away some unfortunate fellow, ricochet off a gun, etc. It's, in my opinion, the most wickedly advanced ballsitics and damage engine that the industry has seen next to qualitiy titles like War Thunder.
+Crafting! A grindy process that really pays off, crafting allows you to custom build your ships and other materials. Gather materials, build the ship like they would in the real days by whipping up things ranging from the hull frames, knees for deck support and even the ship's stern furnishings if she has them. I do emphasise grindy; however, it really pays off in the end; very, very satisfying to craft your "dream ship" yourself!
+Officers! It's a new update which is really awesome. You can hire officers that join you on your missions and gain "perks" and other skills to help you manage your ship. There's a really hillarious "coward" perk that reduces the battle exit timer by 50% for example. I think it's a cool little addon that allows one to say "we beat them through superior gunnery". :)
Now, the game isn't perfect. Though I love the game, it has a few things to hammer out!
-National diplomacy system isn't perfect. The Devs have very wisely been receptive to the community for demands to reform the system in various ways. Pirate mechanics are unusual; as the pirates are manifested as a nation with extra perks to that of the other nations, and hence they have an actual empire, government, ect which is fairly unusual. Declaring war, making treaties are managed by the larger clans, which can be viewed as not too representative of the nation's majority views.
-UI is minimalistic; it's not hideous, but it isn't exactly attractive either. It could be better, but the devs have prioritized (and quite simply, rightly so) the game mechanics over the UI. Hope you're not too picky over game UI!
-Grindy. Personally, I find Naval Action's ships, ranging from the starter cutter to the largest ship of the line infinitley playable, and hence I really didn't mind the "grind", if you will to get to the higher levels for manning ships. However, if yo're impatient, this game may be a bit slow for you. Grind process is longer than most games!
-Learning curve is long! The game's mechanics are complex, so beware those with a low attention span, heh. The Community as a whole is wonderful in being very helpful to new players, but there's no in-game tutorial or official help guides to get you off your feet. It certainly took  me a while to master the art of "manual sailing" in the square rigged ships.
I'm not sure why the game's been getting mixed reviews as of late. The game is, at its core, a sandbox age of sail combat simulator; not a fast and boring free to play like World of Warplanes, etc. The game is designed to create a beautiful and immersive enviroment to engage in combat and screw around in the open world first and foremost; the devs here didn't design the game to advance fast, or the goal of the game to get to the "top level". AS a combat simulator, the game excells beyond any doubt. Anyone who analyzes the game from my perspective will agree wtih me. However, those who analyze the game from those whose interpretation of the nature of the game is to level up and win as quickly as they can will look on the game poorly.
Please keep that in mind when looking at other reviews that attack the grinding of the game and "ganking" mechanics.
Edit: July 30th, 2016
I've also noticed a lot of criticism against the devs apparently not "adding much to the game". In a mere month, they've done the following:
-Added Fishing, hence expanding the economy, adding new roles to trader ships and yet another way to play Naval Action.
-Added Food Rations and other supplies to represent need for resources to mantain crew.
-Crew is now a resource. Losing 50 men to a close range rake now has much more effect on your well being.
-Added officers, a very significant addition to the game.
-Added treasure hunting for some exploration fun.
-Added some new upgrades.
-Added the wonderful 2nd rate ship of the line Bucenature.
-Showcased the Santa Cecilia, a new frigate in the game.
Look at the patch notes for the month, and tell me again that the devs aren't adding much to the game...

The Lego game we always wanted.
The game plays like your standard TT Lego game, combat and stud collecting. The Differance comes as this is a sandbox Lego game, and everything ingame is made from Legos (destructabled, and digable, unlike the standard stagnet Lego game background). The worlds are randomly generated using a seed, with a "micro" build showing you a general idea of what the world is going to be like.
Combat. This is done is done like standard TT Lego games. You have a heart health bar, and basic character attacks. Skeletons are the main type of monster you'll currently face, and you have to beat villian characters to unlock.  Upon being defeated the player, enemy, or vehicle breaks apart. You do have weapons unlocks ingame (The bazooka can level anything), some being powerful, some being a banana. Aiming tends to be a little harder as the character doesn't attack the nearest, instead attacking the end of the mouse pointer. Also, you can climb or crawl about any surface.
Unlocks. Currently the game has only a few of the planned items ingame (Still quite alot). I have yet to see or hear anything about "special" bricks (typical for TT's Lego games, red block can give you bonus studs or abilities). You find weapons and item in chests (ability items like Binoculars don't currently work), after you have collected all currently ingame, the chests start giving lots of studs. Studs are used to unlock the things you have found, just like other TT Lego games. In game there are characters to unlock, not many right now, but they are from the "Minifigures" line giving great customizing option for both male and female. Unlocks include; Items, Vehicles, Animals (yes you can ulock and ride a dragon), Sets (actual lego sets), Brick Builds (basic structures), and props (plants, fences, ect.).
Open World. This is the big differance between the standard TT games, and makes the title worth the EA price alone. I have yet to find any limit in world except digging down, I have heard of people flying quite a distance in all other direction with no wall. The world isn't a stagnet background, its there in front of you, and built with legos (even the water). I haven't found anything that can't be destroyed. Its like having free reign over a lego world. The world feels like with a little work you could make a world that would rival one in the Lego Movie.
Building. Free building is the most difficult part of the game, while really not hard, it can be very overwhelming at times with its power. You can manipulate the train with some terrain tools, and you also have a free build mode with ALOT of lego elements, colors, and designs. I have't gotten to far into building just yet, but what I have played with are amazing. It would be nice if they added Lego IPs to the game; Ninjago, Ultra Agents, Monster Fighters, ect....
Multiplayer. None yet, it has been discussed. In my opinion, that would be the best thing they could add to this game for future features. Looking forward to it.
Lego Digital Designer Software & Steam Workshop. For those of us that use it, its compatable with Lego Worlds, you can bring /Some/ models into the game. With future implementation, this could be the greatest feature the game can have. LDD is software used to make digital Lego models inside a modeling program that's easy to use. That will mean lots of custom models being downloaded from steam, and brought ingame.
Goals. Currently none, no quests, nothing. But plans to have goals implemented are in the works
Cons. You will get game stutter after traveling alot and seeing the open wold, but for me it was never a constent thing, happening maybe once an hour. Camera, you view is indepentant of your character and does not follow behind, and has to be moved indepentant of movment, and while diving or flying while in motion alows very little movement to the camera. Opions, not too many mostly just basic grafics settings right now. Opimazation and a few camera options are the biggest need for the game.
Lego games have always held your had and walked you through a story, now they are alowing you to build your own world. With more tools, this has the promise to be one of the best sandbox building games ever. Even at the current price of $15 this game is more than worth it in its current EA state. Price for features this game rocks AAA titles, and would give it 4.5 stars out of 5.

This game is bad.
You might think that the game is good (the hundreds of joke reviews and gifting is probably the cause of this). You might think that the game is just ok, and unfairly demonized in this hyperbolic age of the internet we live in. You might even think this game is so bad that it's enjoyable, like The Room or Troll II or anything by Neil Breen.
It's not.
If there's one thing that I could use to describe this game, it's painful. For one, it looks hideous. Ugly, sewerish colour pallate masking awful renderings of rats and cats that just looks... unfinished. It's not even like the subject matter is the problem either. Look at Ratatouille. Look at any scene in the rats underground lair, or their hiding hole in attic. Just because the colours were dark, doesn't mean they were ugly. Every colour meshed with each other, and anything important stood out from the background. Things popped. The main characters looked like rats, sure, but they had charm, they had form. These rats just look half-baked. On top of that, some of the designs are borderline offensive, like the rat that dresses in a turban, beard, and suicide vest. And that's what this game is: offensive.
The audio is atrocious. The soundrack is grating and repetitive, the sound effects are canned and just... off. I'd put more effort into this review, but these developers clearly didn't put any effort, so why should I?
The worst part, by far, is gameplay. This isn't that hard to do, a simple rube goldberg machine. 12 year olds have been perfecting this genre 10 years ago on newgrounds. Why make this a 3D game if you're just going to keep everything on a 2D plane? Why make the game in 2D if the game engine allows the ball to fall off the front and back ends of the platforms. Why is the physics engine so awful when you can just use the built-in engine you probably freebooted to make this game? The problem these guys have is that they went ahead that they made a game about making iterations, which requires that if an object (or rat) does a thing, it'll do the same thing every single time. But it doesn't. The physics are soooo inconsistent. How will I know if sending the ball to that batting rat will send the ball flying towards where I want, or flying off the plane of existence the rest of the game is, because currently there's at least a 20% chance of that happening. That's a tip for all you budding developers out there: the chance of that happening should be zip. zero.
There is nothing worthwhile about this game, although it is gratifying to complain about, I guess. If you have this because some friend gave it to you, I'm terribly sorry.

This is, oddly, about space marines, the giant spac ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s from the warhammer 40k universe.  It captures the spirit of the sace marines perfectly- as the greatest warriors in the galaxy, you and your squad can happily march into entire armies of grenskins orks without dying, and the weapons you hold are completely and gleefully overpowered.
The combat of itself is very satisfying, enemies exploding and being mauled by the (not that) large amoury. The overall best weapon is the jump -pack, which allows you to leap into the air and slam down again, exploding all enemies -its just so satisfying!
Also, the space marines actually act like actual space marines instead of just big soldiers- things like not dying, being overpowered XD.
My problems with this game are almost non-existent, but here they are anyway-
The bolter feels slightly weak compared to its lore- it works like a super-heavy machine gun, but even so the shots have less impact than i would like (a note for fans of Warhammer- this is cos the shots dont actually explode, which would have been vsion impairing but cool)
All the energy weapons - plasma gun/pistol, thunder hammer,power axe - have the same sort of blue effect, which is a minor worry tbh.
The basic enemies waste far too much ammo, and the bolter carries far too little - i know orks being very tough is lore frindly, but it takes nearly a full clip of 30 rounds to kill 4 and you only have a 330 ammo cap.
Although i am against discrimination, the space marines in warhammer are supposed to be borderline facist, for the sake of protecting humanity. But captain titus loves everyone and everyone loves captain titus- seriously he acts like a bloody saint.
Overall though, and i know the cons section is bigger than the pros btw, but i like complainging about nice things, this game is extremely fun, well presented and satisfying.
While a bit repetitive, it definitely gives you the weight, impact and atmosphere that you expect from playing a Space Marine. Had a blast with it.

While it is fun in a play-it-while-doing-something-else way, it's extremely simplistic. On one hand it's easy to pick up and play, on the other... well, no, you can play this entire game on one hand. It's arrow keys + numpad0 (or WASD + space) for driving and using pickups, and apart from aggressive drafting, shortcuts and strategic dropping of mines there's not much else you can do. Perhaps that's why the events took me 103 minutes total to complete, including frequent restarts to get gold medals/beat my one friend on the leaderboard's scores. Most of it felt kind of inane, with the AI rarely giving much of a challenge outside of seemingly random selections of events, where the they-can-push-you-but-not-vice-versa physics got me stuck on obstacles or the random pickup system decided to take me uphill.
+ Can play with one hand
+ Quick events
+ Decent music (though very repetitive)
+ Handling is alright
- Very short
- Inconsistent AI
- Pickups turn some events into a slot machine
- You unlock boss vehicles that you can't use
- Bad car/car collision physics (e.g. picked one of the heaviest vehicles and still couldn't push other cars at all)
- Time trials are full of mines for no reason
- No rebinding of anything
Consider the price of this, then the price of Motorstorm RC, a game that lasts much longer for less money.

A solid story with a charming, quirky art style reminiscent of old school RPGs. This game is good for fans of interactive storytelling, point and click adventures, or just quality writing.
My only knocks are (1) the questionable pathing around many of the levels, and (2) the pacing of the story.
For my tastes, the level pathing has too many twists and turns seemingly for no reason other than to be complex. The controls in general are on the weak side, whether using keyboard (recommended) or mouse (NOT recommended).
The pacing of the story is a bit draggy. It is redeemed by the overall high quality of the story, but there are areas of the game that feel disjointed, and occasionally I wondered how long it would take for me to uncover a meaningful piece of the mystery. Much of the first half of the game can feel meaningless and tedious since you really have no idea what's going on. Maybe it's just me, but the game could benefit by a bit of tightening up.
Still highly recommended, especially when it goes on sale in summer or for the holidays.

There were games that I looked forward to playing but then it turn out to be a dissapointment. This one is actually the other way around, I thought this might be something that I don't like, but it might be a good educational game to play with kids.  But after half an hour into the game, I was really surprised that not only I like this game, I love it.
This game is not only fun, but funny as well.  In a nutshell, you help people by creating 'objects' or add an adjective to something, then you get a star.  So you go around and help people, and you clear stages/area around the world.  Like I mentioned, it's actually good to play around kids.  When you think about it, the whole theme of the game is about helping people, so not only it seems educational, it is also a nice game to play with kids.
What I really like about the game is the freedom to express your imagination, and there is always more than one way to do things here.  Before I played this game, I have this preconception that this is one of those game that is very linear, you have to use the right word for anything; but, that's totally not the case here, the flexibility of this game truly amazed me.  Also, I like the vast amount of objects you can create, combined with different adjectives.  It almost seems like there is infinite possiblities of objects you can create in this game(hence the name, "Unlimited"?).
I also love the humour in this game, lots of pop culture reference, it's like lots of spoofs from movies and such.  And it gets better if you are the type of person like me who like to create objects that make the situation even funnier.
This game is generally easy, but sometimes it can make you think really hard.  So if you don't know what objects or adjectives to add, you can always move on to do another one.  That brings me to another thing I like about this, you can play this game at your own pace.  You don't have to spend certain amount of time in one sitting.  You can even spend like 1 minute in this game, maybe help one guy, save the game, and come back later to play more.
There really isn't any story to this game, I technically finished the game under 10 hours and saw the 'ending'  by collecting 60 stars, but there seem to be a total of 106 stars.  I will probably play till I get all of the stars.  This is my first Scribblenauts game, I will definately play more of other Scribblenauts games.

There is sooo much to say about this game but i'll try to keep this short and simple
1. Gameplay: The gameplay welcomes both newbies with fighting games by providing a training mode to practice what moves do what and to see all the blockbusters (AKA supers) that each character has, and veterans to fighting games by practicing combos, speaking of which the combo system is INSANE, by providing the ability to go over 100 hit combos, but back to the practice mode, veteran can practice their hit marks by applying hit boxes, blocking only, etc., with the inclusion of a menu saying how much damage a certain move does, how long said move stuns the player, how much health the player has, all that good stuff.
2. Characters: Each character in the game has their own story mode and can be playable in arcade mode. The game has 8 characters which is very little for a fighting game, but the game is getting DLC characters with their own story mode, one of which has already been fully released (AKA Squigly). Each character has their own attributes, Peacock is a projectile type character, Cerebella does more damage but slower than some others, Double has the ability to morph into other characters and yeah.
3. Story: Story is simple, there is a heart called the Skullheart that can grant any girl a wish, but one that has a impure soul turns into a rage maniac called the Skullgirl, which one has been turned into one, it's up to one of the 8 (9 if you include the DLC character) to get to the Skullgirl and Skullheart
4. Music: If you’re a fan of jazzy tunes, then the music is up your alley. The music is composed by Michiru Yamane, the same person that did the Castlevania: Symphony of the Night soundtrack, so if you’re a fan of that, you might be a fan of this.
5. Art: If you are an artist then you will love this. Each character frames is singly animated, which means roughed drawn, polished, and then colored. The art of the game is supposed to resemble a "Dark Deco" style art.
6. Multiplayer: The multiplayer has modes such as lobbies for the group that wants to fight each other or a quick match mode for those who wants as it says, a quick match.
Final Thoughts: This game is a great starter for anyone who wants to get into fighting games and it also appeals to veterans by adding a really good combo system. The only downside of the game is the lack of characters which I hope Lab Zero will add more, and they will because it says so in the feature DLC section in the game description. All and all, it’s a good game that you should pick up and have a go.

It's like a third person perspective of what went on in your mind as a kid when thinking of what you could do with more lego.

Disclaimer: I have more hours logged on my alternate account.
Lego Worlds is a cutesy game that allows you to do what you could do in real life, but with twists. The controls are much like the existing Lego games, but in this, you don't have any specific tasks. You can generate random worlds, share the worlds with your friends via universal code, or save and load worlds from your hard drive. You can choose your Lego minifigure, which you have 3 of initially, before starting the world. As you play in the open world, you discover new creatures, characters, and vehicles. Though you can interact with the ones in the world already, you can also spawn new ones. There are many tools to build, change the terrain, and select pre-built models.
+The characters are very unique, and some of them have different abilities
+You can ride any animal you encounter
+The driving mechanics are very smooth
+The tools are easy to build with
+There are many different animals that spawn randomly in the world
+Eight (?) different biomes to discover
+Treasure chests!
-The camera sometimes wanders off of your character
-The camera can be very hard to control
-After building, it is possible to spawn in a dangerous place/in the ground and die
-Tools can sometimes break and not work correctly
Overall, I would give this game a 9.4/10. I am satisfied with the amount of detail in it, especially for $15. It is perfect for children and adults who grew up owning and loving Lego sets. I'm glad they didn't mess this game up (so far), because right now it is great. If the tools were improved and the controls were smoother, it would be a 10/10.

I wish there was a middle ground between recommending and not recommending, but until such time as that exists, I will stick to my status of 'not-recommending'. But with some positive points.
Allow me to clarify:
I see a lot of positive reviews for this game, and I know it was a product of its era, but I really struggle to wrap my brain around this one. Aside from a few issues where save games were mysteriously deleted, I found that before I could get my hands on a campaign mission I had to wade through inane emergency after inane emergency.
Quick! Someone's had a fall and has a minor injury! (A minor injury? Like a sprained ankle? Fine, they can wait while I tend to the three fires going on and the pickpocket on the loose) - I return a minute or two later and find that the person had DIED from their minor injury
I eventually did get into the campaign and tried the first two 'levels' - but really it seems that there is a formula for dealing with them, and deviating *at all* makes things difficult.
Pathfinding is ridiculous - roads are a mere suggestion - and I know there's the ages-old argument about depth vs simplicity, but requesting a fire truck, then waiting for it, then selecting it when it arrives, then clicking near to the fire emergency, then asking your firefighters to get out, then asking your firefighters to equip themselves with fire hoses, then asking your firefighters to attach their equipped fire hoses to separate fire hydrants dotted around the area, THEN finally asking them to put out the fire (Though the hitbox often means you end up cooling a building and not attacking the fire), it does get rather tiresome. When the fire is out , reasonably you'd expect them to tackle any other fires in their immediate vicinity, but no, they will stand about and wait for the order - often while you're doing other things - so the fire spreads yet further. THEN once the fire is out, you tell your firefighters to disconnect the hoses, put the gear away, then get back in the vehicle before either shuttling them to the next fire or sending them back to HQ.
It is very difficult to manage time in this game, and completing campaigns often means failing them often enough until you know the formula. It's a very stressful game at the best of times!
I really can see the appeal, and Hardcore RTS fans may very well be all over this, but this game is not for me, and certainly not one I'd recommend for the casual or average gamer...!
THAT ALL SAID - apparently there are plenty of mods which make this game a lot more playable. To those who have time for such endeavours - I wish you luck!

I purchased Game Dev Tycoon when it was first released, and still hop into it every now and then. In fact I am getting hooked into it once again after booting it up in Steam just now (I always played with the stand-alone launcher before). There's something really charming about the game, starting as a small-time developer in your garage and building your company into something you might see from large developers today. It's relaxing to play, with no stress involved, but is far more in-depth than you may think upon first glance.
I think it's the retro feel at the beginning that I like the most, being able to almost relive the 80's video game scene and recreate your favorite games, even mimicking a company if you'd like. My favorite playthrough, in fact, was when I developed all of my games based on the original Fighting Fantasy adventure gamebooks series. Then again, I've also set up a silly company that focused on XXX-themed games with ridiculous premises and horrible storylines. It failed miserably, but it was a lot of fun.
That's the thing about the game, it allows you to explore any ideas you come up with, and it also gets you into a great creative space. Anyone who has played Game Dev Tycoon has uttered to themselves at one point or another while developing a game within the game, "Man that actually would make a great game, I wish I could make it in real life."
The only slight drawback to Game Dev Tycoon in my eyes is the fact that there are specific parameters in place for the scores your created games will receive. Once you understand the formulas (or if you follow someone's guide perhaps), you have a better shot at doing well, and it could take some creativity out of the process. That's why I wouldn't recommend reading any guides at first, it's best to find it all out on your own. Even after understanding what those parameters are, though, you will still enjoy yourself.
I still hold out hope for a sequel, as there are certainly ways to improve this game, but until then Game Dev Tycoon will likely eat up a lot of your time as you drift off into a creative space or relive the golden age.

I'm a fan of Micro Machines 2: Turbo Tournament. And this game reminds me of it.
Toybox Turbos is a Micro Machines game without its license. There are all the core elements of the series: toy cars, crazy tracks, speed and the duel mode, where you  must race faster than your rival in order to get him out of the screen and score a point.
There's a fun single player career mode, where you have to select different types of cars, choosing from bulldozers, sportcars, trucks, etc with different characteristics and driving styles. The sense of progression is good, you have to earn in-game coins (fortunately, there aren't microtransactions) to unlock new rides and for every championship you have a boss to defeat in duel. Even if the AI is simplicistic and the general difficulty is low, this title engages you with all the different playmodes that has to offer: from Time Attack to standard race with weapons it's a fun to play especially with friends, whenever it's local or online multiplayer.
Techincally speaking, the game offers nice visuals, consider it like a more polished mobile game. Even the controls are responsive and you can feel the difference when driving all the 35 cars.

Codemasters has a very deep game development history.  One that includes the inspiration for Toybox Turbos, Micro Machines.  I was a big fan of the Micro Machines game on my Sega Genesis, but it was one I never fully completed, both because it was a rental game (back when you had to go to a rental store and have the game back in a couple days) and because it became exceptionally difficult toward the end for my childhood self.   So twenty some odd years later, I was pretty excited to find out there was a spiritual successor to that wonderful game of my past.
Jumping in to Toybox Turbos, you quickly notice the aesthetic is thoroughly Micro Machines.  Similar to the 1991 classic, all races take place with tiny vehicles on tracks comprised of many household objects including things like children's toys, kitchen utensils and dishes, and pool tables.  You take the wheel of a wide variety of vehicles that have varying stats that are part of what are basically ranks.  The first set of races allows you five or so fairly slow cars that you take around some simple tracks that I found to be pretty easy to win.  Yet as you complete these different sets of races, each iterative set will feature faster vehicles and more treacherous tracks that will have you skidding, jumping, and narrowly avoiding pitfalls.  You may find winning a breeze early on but the sets of races toward the end will be more difficult.
There are a small variety of race types that range from your straightforward four car multi lap race to you one where you are outrunning a deadly wave while speeding around the track for as far as possible before it catches up to you.   They seem very unique at first, but the gameplay pretty much always calls for you to get around a track going as fast as possible, much like any racing game.
I found myself really enjoying the nostalgia the aesthetic created along with responsive controls and reasonably varied gameplay.  The collection of cars you get to mess around with has a some fun designs in it and I was wanting more just to unlock and use them rather than only getting whichever one had the best stats for me.  You can even do a small amount of paint customization on each vehicle to personalize it if that's your thing.  The tracks feature a great level of detail and some of the small additions like paperclips, marbles, and buttons are set up in a way that you can push them around and feel like you're having an impact on the crazy tiny world.  It's a shame they obviously weren't able to get Micro Machines on board to fully realize an iterative version of the original.  However, the recent release of Micro Machines World Series shows that apparently it takes more than just brands to make a good game.
There aren't many complaints on my end for this game.  I thought there was going to be a major issue when it crashed repeatedly on startup, but I found a post in the Discussion section of the game's Steam page that stated that you just needed to set your desktop resolution to 720p, launch the game, and then set it to your normal desktop resolution.  Then you can go back and set your desktop resolution to what it was before and the game will launch normally.   I assume there is some issue with the default resolution that it tries to launch in, which is an odd issue not to have resolved for a game that released three years ago.  But fixing it was simple enough that I quickly forgot about it.  My biggest complaint is that the standard camera mode is a bit weak.  You can swap it to a top down mode that is the worst thing ever or a retro top down mode that is much more reminiscent of the original Micro Machines game, but is probably a little less useful because of how it limits your view forward on the track.  In general, it's best just to get used to the standard camera mode and hope it doesn't mess you up at a bad time.  Also, don't expect to be able to play online multiplayer.  That's rare for a lot of online multiplayer in games three years out though.
Toybox Turbos is quite simply a fun game that will tug at your nostalgia strings if you were a fan of the original game.  It should be pretty easy to get in to for most players and the difficulty doesn't ramp up too quickly, so it rarely bogs down unless you're after perfection for each race.  Even being a bit of an older game, I recommend picking it up if you have the chance, especially if you can get it for a few bucks on sale rather than for its base price.

I have to say that this game is not what I expected.  I expected a game where the player travels back in the old man's memories, and gives him a chance to relive his life - thus allowing the player to play through the man's life and make changes in it.  That is not the case at all.
To the Moon IS NOT A GAME!  It would be more accurately described as an interactive story. No, not a choose your own ending kind of story. The story is very linear, follows a laid out path and conclusion.  The player is not often offered a choice, and even when he is, it doesn't matter.  You can only follow one path, and that is that.  As such, not only is To the Moon a story rather than a game, it posesses no replay value.
So, is it worth buying? Yes, definitely.  Even though the graphics look like it came from the mid-1990s, the story is compelling, and the music beautiful.  It's a tear-jerker, and I often felt myself wanting to go through "just one more scene".
To the Moon has no keybinding controls, and even though that is a big bugbear of mine, its controls are bound to the number pad, not WASD. As a left-handed person, well done development team.
Also, there is no volume control for the music. Sole control over volume comes from your own speakers or headset.
In short, To the Moon is not a game, has no replay value, no control bindings, and no volume control.  But its compelling story and beautiful music more than compensate.  Definitely worth the price of admission.

Very short version:
If you love 2D platformers then is this game a must have! Probably the best platformer we will get in 2015.
Short version:
Beautiful visuals (graphics and animation)
Amazing music
Sad story (unless you have a frozen heart)
Fun 2D platformer gameplay
Hard game but not unfair
Long version:
There have always been a question about if games would ever reach a point where we can call it “art” (like movies are a work of art), but this game would be the kind I would show if such a talk should ever happen as it have everything there makes a game amazing: Amazing visuals, a good soundtrack of very talented people and a sad story to follow up on (there was moments where I almost shed a tear or just felt very sad about the characters in the story), all this boils down to a very amazing experience and you want  to figure out how it all turns out.
But not only is the game’s presentation amazing but the gameplay itself is very fun! The game slowly gives you power-ups there opens up the map to find secrets or other power-ups that you were not able to reach, which will make you go back to get them all and explore areas that you already had visited before. And even better is that even though you are getting a lot of power-ups then doesn’t it feel hard to execute them (mouse and keyboard) which makes it smooth to play. I was only troubled when I did a double jump instead of a wall jump at times but it didn’t happen too often.
One thing to notice is this game is hard! Expect to die a lot! But with that said is the game not unfair as it having a very clever use of save points. You can at any time use energy (your attack resource) to create a save point so when you die will you return to this point. So if you reach a area there looks hard or you just got through a difficult segment then is it easy to just place a save point. The system also gives amazing exit points as you can just place down a save point and then close the game and return later.
Overall will I say this is probably one of the best 2D platformers ever made and is a must buy if you are a big fan of 2D platformers! Do not miss out on this amazing game!

This game have good graphics and solid gameplay in terms of naval combat in the Age of Sail genre. Actually the best what you can find and thus it is the reason why I purchase it.
I can't give it full points, despite the only game in its  genre fulfulling all the mechanics and solid, smooth gameplay.
This game is extremely time consuming. Prepare to have a book while playing this game, because it is very slow paced. The naval battles are fine, but the Open World experience is something most people want to be revamped.
There are numerous other reasons why this game doesn't favour casual gamers and is more geared towards hardcore gamers. It is time consuming, limited features in economy which could be improved upon, time consuming and long distances to sail. Expect to spend more or less an hour in the Open World before arriving at a certain port or battle location.
Also note the devs are a small group and take very long to implement updates. An update each month and then patches in the upcoming weeks. Much more could be desired and feedback is only considered from hardcore longtime standing players, making it difficult for new casual gamers to fit in.
Good graphics, solid gameplay, but favour too much to hardcore gamers, bland economy and time consuming. 6/10.

In the time I played I never felt a connection to anything. Big wide open spaces, npc ships. It felt like a lot of effort to go somewhere that looks and feels the same as every other spot. The water was not exciting. No big battles with giant whitecapping waves, rocking the ships, making you fight the waves and time your shots. Instead it feels arcady. Wind should change during battle... why remove reality, when it would be a solid addition to the gameplay mechanics?
I love that you can see the shore now in battle, and use it as a tool. This makes the wind direction actually important (wind that changed direction could be a real challange).
Remaining in aiming view when looking around that ship would really help keep the immersion in battle, but instead looking around to get your bearings is penalized with a game mechanic that is a little jolting.
What I would give for life to be in the ocean and land to look at as I walk along the line of my ship, maybe even enter my cabin, as the men run about taking care of the ship.
Important things to keep the immersion, as most of the time in the game is spent in transition from one place to another. Instead we can only look at a stripped down version of our actual ship, dead seas, and calm sailing, with storms so weak they are easily missed.
There is potential here, the question is: will it be realised? I think it is imporant for developers to listen to the community and seriously consider if they are doing the right thing or not.

Maybe hang on a bit before getting this game. It has brilliant potential but right now it's just a concept. If it gets multiplayer (it better get multiplayer, that would make it something infinitely playable rather than a fun toy that gets old after few weeks) and the ability to build your own vehicles rather than just the pre-built ones, and maybe a simple questing or brick-hunting system to keep things interesting, this has the potential to be my favourite game of all time.

First and foremost, there are some things about this game that are VERY well done...
PROS:
<> Awesome graphics - the movements, the models and everything else looks well polished
<> Great amount of customization - you can customize your character in-game using pieces from all the people you find
But the things that are lacking are numerous, and easily make this a waste of money at this particular time...
CONS:
<> The controls suck - the basic movement isn't terrible, but trying to drive a car is extremely frustrating with a keyboard and mouse. Camera angles also frequently become a problem as you get a face-full of lego bricks instead of what's directly in front of your character.
<> There's nothing to do - At night the skeletons come out, but never fear... they can't hurt you unless you're seriously stupid, or intending to be hurt. Just clicking one a swarm of these guys one at a time will end in 100% success - no injuries and all the skeletons die.
<> Building is limit-less. It's great to have options, but when you can cover literally an entire land mass in new bricks within 5 minutes of starting a game, the entire process becomes trivial. You don't need to earn bricks right now, which I find silly. Also, once you unlock buildings you can place them indefinitely anywhere you like - the same goes for vehicles... you can endlessly spawn them until you have a mountain of cars and boats. It's amusing the first time, but then the cheap-ness of it all sets in...
All in all, there's a lot of potential here, and since I already bought this game I'm rooting for them to do something with it... but right now it's not much fun. It's worth perhaps an hour of somewhat enthused play, but after that you're going to wonder why you spent fifteen dollars on that hour of amusement. Also, why is Lego releasing an early access game? I feel like they have the money to avoid half-baked concepts like this one. Anyway... here's to hoping things get better, it's only day one after all (although considering this is Lego, that doesn't bode well...)

I received this game as a birthday gift a few years ago, and recently I was searching my game library for something to review. This popped up and I instantly downloaded it. I knew the game was great material for a bad review, so I took the chance.
I'm a level in, and the game's already as boring as staring into space for 6 hours straight. Basically, the main objective in-game is to use the rats to kill cats. After you've successfully killed the cat(s), your mission (level) is complete. Oh, did I mention this game promotes animal abuse? Now, I'm not the kind of person to go around being an SJW about things, but this really caught my attention when I first acquired the game. You're killing animals to complete levels. Pretty PETA-worthy, right? I guess I'm wrong, since this game is still alive and well.
For a game created in 2009, the graphics are utterly horrible. You'd expect the visual quality to be nicer than what it really is, but they lost an opportunity. The game automatically launches in windowed mode, and that itself is more annoying than the actual game. This is the only game that has this feature, and I haven't messed around with the settings enough to know if the game even
a full-screen mode.
There are three difficulties to choose from-- Tutorial (Easy-mode with tutorial enabled), Normal, and Expert. Since I wanted to start off fresh, and play seriously, I booted up in the 'Tutorial' mode. I was greeted by an insanely cringey text-to-speech bot, who gave me directions on how to play the game correctly, and complete the first level. After completing the first level, I transitioned to Normal mode. The same thing, just no cringey bot telling you what to do.
There is really nothing else left to say about this game, it's a piece of crap, and if you're actually considering purchasing this joke that the developers call a game, then suit yourself. I warned you, this game is nothing more than a dust-collector sitting in my game library. Enough said.
There's a reason this game is originally $0.99, and that's because the developers definitely rushed on this title. This game could've been a little better than what the end result turned out to be. There is apparently a second
game, and I have yet to get it. Probably sometime in the future, when I am at my wit's end, and I have nothing else better to review, I'll get the game. It'll be for comedic relief, though, I can tell you that.
